candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Berlin sculptor Kwade installs mirrored architectural interventions in the prison yard; her interest in perception meets colonial ruin.

candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong positions itself as a neutral terminus for circulating antiquities, this time from Cairo.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Hong Kong as global loan destination

candidates.title: Treasures of the Mughal Court from the Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.blurb: V&A loans Mughal miniatures and jade; HKPM continues mapping China within Eurasian luxury networks.
candidates.why_shortlisted: thematic coherence with HKPM's curatorial line

candidates.title: The Forbidden City and The Palace of Versailles: China-France Cultural Encounters
candidates.blurb: Jesuits, porcelain, and court portraiture trace the axis of early modern diplomacy before the modern museum.
candidates.why_shortlisted: East-West encounter narrative with archival depth

candidates.title: A Movable Feast: The Culture of Food and Drink in China
candidates.blurb: Ceramics, paintings, and ritual vessels track taste as statecraft; design professionals will note the vitrines.

candidates.title: Wonders of Imperial Carpets: Masterpieces from the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
candidates.blurb: Silk Road textiles on loan from Qatar; Hong Kong curates continuity between Persian and Qing design traditions.
candidates.why_shortlisted: luxury goods and cross-cultural trade focus

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: Met loans global jewellery; HKPM frames personal adornment as a universal language for its luxury-adjacent audience.

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection
candidates.blurb: Private collection of Chinese textiles becomes public; a case study in how Hong Kong absorbs diaspora capital culturally.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong's collateral pavilion returns home; the local iteration tests how Venice work reads without the Giardini frame.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Survey of current Hong Kong practice; the museum stakes a claim to define what local contemporaneity looks like.

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Export porcelain and trade paintings from a Hong Kong collector; the city revisits its own formation as an interface.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Hong Kong's historical role in global trade

candidates.title: Tai Kwun Neon Connection
candidates.blurb: Permanent neon installation in Tai Kwun Lane; nostalgia for the city's vanishing sign trade formalised as heritage.
candidates.why_shortlisted: neon as Hong Kong's vernacular design
